newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH FINMIN WANTS BANKING LAW QUICKLY ADOPTED.
newsitem.headline: POLISH FINMIN WANTS BANKING LAW QUICKLY ADOPTED.

text.p: Poland's finance minister, responding to criticism that the government is delaying work on a new draft banking law, said on Wednesday he would like the bill approved as quickly as possible.
"The banking law is one of our priorities... Its first reading should take place at parliament's next session," the minister, Marek Belka, told a news conference.

He said he hoped legislators would manage to pass the crucial bill before general elections due around September, because otherwise the new government and parliament could start work on the draft law afresh, further delaying its passage.

Eearlier this month, the central bank's head Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz alleged the government was neglecting the banking bill and was concerned only about a new central bank charter, which would give it powers to decide who would sit on some policy-making boards.
But Belka said the government wanted parliament to scrutinise the two bills jointly.
"We would like it (the banking law) and the law on the National Bank of Poland examined together," he said.

The draft banking law would bring Poland's banking system closer to Western standards. It would provide for creating an independent body for banking supervision and guarding against unfair competition between banks.
It would also regulate more closely the origins of bank capital and the ownership structures of banks, preventing the dangerous expansion of so-called internal loans.
The central bank, which helped draft the bill, says it d would make banks safer for Poles and help accumulate savings deposits, which would in future be used to finance Poland's economic growth.
